SYS2 "Historian": {"name": "Historian", "asset_type": "IT", "past_incidents": "A flood of requests stopped it in 2024", "technology_used": ["OSIsoft PI"]}

STRIDE CATEGORIES:
- Spoofing: pretending to be another user, device or service to be trusted as them.
- Tampering: unauthorised modification of data, configuration, commands or code.
- Repudiation: an action that cannot be reliably attributed to whoever performed it.
- Information Disclosure: information exposed to someone not authorised to see it.
- Denial of Service: a service or capability made unavailable or degraded.
- Elevation of Privilege: gaining access or rights beyond those that were granted.
For EVERY candidate slot decide whether that threat genuinely applies to this asset and landscape, in the asset's sector, sub-sector and critical service, and under which of its own listed "categories". It applies only if it can affect the asset itself or at least one listed system, is technically plausible for the technology and interfaces described, an attacker could plausibly carry it out, and it belongs to at least one of its listed categories. Do not change the candidate's type or threat, and never add a category it does not list.
It applies only if the attacker acts on the asset or a listed system: preparation done elsewhere (searching public sources, obtaining or building tools, setting up infrastructure) is not a threat to this asset.
A threat belongs to one of its listed categories only when one of its own actions (every action its name states is its own) directly causes the loss the STRIDE category line describes, on the asset or a listed system. If it would reach that loss only through an added step that is not part of the threat (for example a data theft put under Tampering by also altering the records it copies), it does not belong to that category: leave that category out; relevant=false only when it belongs to none of its listed categories. An action that only obtains a credential, secret or session (stealing or phishing credentials, stealing a session) only enables later actions: its own loss is the stolen secret exposed (Information Disclosure), and anything later done with it is an added step. Only when the threat's name states the credential, account or session is used (for example "takeover", "misuse", "abuse"; "theft" and "phishing" are not use) is that use its own action, which may cause Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege or any other loss the use itself directly causes.
CANDIDATE ATOMICITY: Each candidate slot is ONE threat; never combine or borrow fields across candidates.
Judge against the RECORDED facts: a fact the landscape does not state is UNKNOWN, not absent. Unknown is not evidence that a threat exists, and unknown is not evidence that it does not exist. Do not reject a threat solely because a DETAIL of a recorded technology is unrecorded (for example whether its default password was changed or how it is patched), but require the threat to independently satisfy the asset, technology, interface, attacker-plausibility and STRIDE rules. When an unknown detail is necessary for acceptance, state the assumption explicitly as "assumes ...".
An assumption may fill a missing detail of a technology the asset or a listed system is recorded to have; it may never assume that a technology, component or device exists. If the threat needs one that no recorded fact of the asset or a listed system mentions (for example an LLM, a cloud service, a billing system, an engineering workstation, a jump server, a wireless or radio link, removable media), list it in "needs".
The ORGANISATION line is background only: never accept a threat because the organisation uses a technology elsewhere; it must fit the asset's or a listed system's own recorded facts.
DECISION RULE: decide `relevant` by the rules above alone; a high impact, likelihood or confidence never makes a threat that fails them relevant.
Every verdict, relevant or not, carries its reasons. Each reason is ONE sentence of at most 25 words that names the systems by NAME as written in the landscape, never by alias (SYS1, SYS2 ...), and states any assumption made. For each category a relevant threat belongs to, its reason says why the threat fits: what in the asset's or the systems' recorded role, technology, interfaces or data, or the sector's attacker motive, makes it plausible, and how its own action causes that category's loss; it never retells the attack steps. For one that does not apply, it says why not.

For a relevant threat, "categories" lists only the slot's own categories it belongs to, each name copied exactly, the one its own action most directly causes FIRST, each with its own impact (HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW for the business) and reason. Judge each threat against the asset and all its systems together. For a relevant threat: "systems" lists exactly the systems the threat involves, by alias, one, several or all of them ([] means the asset itself); "entry_points" lists the systems among "systems" through which an attacker could really get in to carry out this threat ([] only when "systems" is []); confidence is an integer 0-100. In every verdict, "needs" lists every component, device or technology the threat requires that no recorded fact of the asset or a listed system mentions (for example "SIEM", "USB ports", "jump server"); [] when everything it requires is recorded. LIKELIHOOD: for a relevant threat, "likelihood" (HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW) is how likely at least one of that slot's own listed attackers would attempt this threat against this asset, judged on what the threat needs (access, skill and resources), the motive this asset's sector and critical service attract, and the exposure the recorded systems show; the more listed attackers who plausibly could, the higher. ACTIONS: for a relevant threat, "actions" lists the concrete acts the threat's NAME states, each a short verb phrase saying what the attacker does to which system, by name. Turn a noun such as "fraud", "theft" or "extortion" into the act itself; acts joined by "and" or "with" are separate acts; alternatives joined by "or" stay one act; words that only describe its target, account or means stay with that act. Give no more acts than the name states.
